Name: hierarchical_feature_extraction
Title: Hierarchical Set Abstraction: Learning Global and Local features of point clouds
Motivation: Point-cloud analysis requires both global shape understanding and fine-grained local detail. Existing methods often focus on one at the expense of the other.
Method: Our pipeline stacks multiple Set Abstraction (SA) and Feature Propagation (FP) modules. Each SA uses FPS sampling and ball-query grouping followed by MLPs to encode local geometry, with a global feature injected at the deepest layer via attention. FP modules then upsample and fuse features through skip-connections. The fused multi-scale features feed into a classification head.
Experiment: In this experiment, we compare the performance of different feature extraction networks, especially considering both gloabl and local features
Summary: Propose a hierarchical set abstraction method to effectively integrate global and local features

Name: relational_geometric_transformer_block
Title: Relational Geometric Transformer Blocks for Hierarchical Point Cloud Understanding
Motivation: Humans perceive 3D objects by decomposing them into meaningful parts and understanding the spatial relationships between these parts. Existing point cloud networks often struggle to capture this hierarchical and relational geometric understanding. Standard attention mechanisms, while effective in capturing dependencies, may not inherently leverage the structured, part-based nature of 3D objects. This research aims to develop a novel block that mimics this human-like perception by explicitly modeling geometric relationships at multiple levels of abstraction.
Method: We propose the Relational Geometric Transformer Block (RGTB). The RGTB operates in two main stages: 1. **Intra-Cluster Geometric Attention:** Points are first grouped into local 'geometric clusters' based on proximity and local surface characteristics (e.g., using a simplified density-based clustering or a learnable grouping mechanism within a neighborhood). Within each cluster, a self-attention mechanism is applied, where the Query, Key, and Value projections are conditioned on the local geometric properties (coordinates, relative positions) of the points. This captures fine-grained geometric features within local parts. 2. **Inter-Cluster Relational Attention:** After aggregating features within clusters, a second, higher-level attention mechanism operates on cluster representatives (e.g., centroids or pooled features). This attention considers the geometric relationships between these cluster representatives (e.g., distance, relative orientation between cluster centroids) to understand how parts are spatially arranged. The Q, K, V projections at this stage are conditioned on these inter-cluster geometric relationships. The RGTB can be stacked hierarchically, allowing for the learning of increasingly abstract geometric relationships. This approach allows the network to learn both local geometric details within object parts and the global structural arrangement of these parts.
Experiment: 1. **RGTB Implementation:** Develop the `RelationalGeometricTransformerBlock` class. This will involve creating sub-modules for geometric clustering (e.g., using ball query and a simple clustering algorithm), intra-cluster attention, and inter-cluster attention. The attention layers will be designed to take point/cluster coordinates and features, and incorporate geometric conditioning into Q/K/V projections. 2. **Integration:** Replace a subset of the Set Abstraction (SA) modules in the `PointNetEncoder` with the RGTB. Experiment with applying RGTBs at different depths of the encoder to explore their effect on feature hierarchy. 3. **Training and Evaluation:** Train the modified model on ModelNet40. Evaluate performance against the baseline PointNet++ and the previous Geometry-Aware Attention idea. Analyze learned cluster formations and inter-cluster relationships to assess the model's ability to capture hierarchical geometric structure. Conduct ablation studies on the geometric conditioning and clustering strategies.
Summary: Introduces Relational Geometric Transformer Blocks that hierarchically model point cloud structure by applying attention within geometrically formed clusters and between cluster representatives, guided by relational geometry.
